questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture and opportunity to do outdoor experiences in nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: To be fair, there is a lot of practicalities and it is an overload of information in the beginning, and the most important things might get lost in the information such as finding cheap accomodation if you're not able to pay a huge amount to stay at a student accommodation (there are other opportunities), creating a bank account and starting to study at a new place. Then again, I dont think there is a smart way to do it, other than emphasising the importance of reading the documents before arrival and be well prepared. It is a big deal to go on exchange - a lot of practicalities, but you grow from that as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a weekly meeting for international students and an intro meeting in the orientation week. I would have liked to know more about how the system works studying in Australia - especially with the assessments and the overall percentage. That would have made everything much easier and less stressful for sure!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have told us more about how the assessment summary works and that it is only a percentage of the full grade and what it takes to pass a course, since it is very different from Denmark and other countries

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Flatmates is soo good! Found some great deals there, especially because many student accommodations only accept students for a minimum of 6 months, and we are only there for 4 months. Using a platform such as flatmates you also get the possibility to live with Australian people your age and is probably the best way to really learn about the culture,

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is easier to become part of the culture in a share house, because on campus there are manu international students, which can be an experience as well. But if you'd like to learn about australian culture off campus is the better choice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Student accommodations are overpriced taking advantage of students desperately needing accommodation from overseas not able to find other alternatives. Once you figure out the housing market you see how much you're paying overprice in a student accommodation such as scape or student one.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You enrolled yourself into courses and you could choose which days you wanted to do the workshops. So smart! so you could pretty much make your own timetable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Phone and other services

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much, it was pretty easy and simple

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty similar - really good professors and tutors. Some better than others of course, but that is how it is. Actually i would describe the teachers as more welcoming and supportive than in UCPH at some level.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Promoting Health through Physical Activity, Exercise and Diet. Nutrition and Exercise. Sports Psychology. Youth, Sport and Physical Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs! I was really surprised in a good way, I joined 3 different clubs (hiking, wakeboarding and sailing club) and had some really good experiences and meeting nice people from all over the world. Can recommend!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join in on some clubs and go explore.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking! go on smaller trips to the beach.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - people are very warm and welcoming

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really - i didnt have succes in that area

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmth of people, the small talk and how much Australians like to help.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Don't be afraid to do things on your own - like joining a club at the uni and go on a hike with them. They're all in the same boat wanting to meet new people
- Engage in physical activity or other hobbies you have, get a membership somewhere and go on a regular basis
- Ask for help if you need it, there are many opportunities to get help at the student service with all the questions you may have

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There're free breakfast and dinner, a shop with cheap grocery stuff for students and so many social arrangements all the time. The Redroom is the uni's own bar!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The feeling of being independent and succeeding in making new friends and completing a semester overseas!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling lonely in the beginning. But concurred it and made some amazing friends through my personal sport.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
